primitives.name: Pass Completion Probability Surface
primitives.verbatim_quote: We introduce a generalized additive model for completion percentages by field location.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p': 'probability of completion, dimensionless', 'x, y': 'field coordinates in yards relative to scrimmage line, dimensionless', '\\beta_i': 'regression coefficients, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Spatial smoothness of pass outcomes; independence of predictors within generalized additive framework.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low sample size near boundary regions or extreme field positions.

layer2.mapping: Maps 2D field locations to pass success probabilities via kernel-smoothed empirical distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Completion rate deviation from league average by coordinate bin.

primitives.name: Naive Bayes Adjustment Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: We use a Naive Bayes approach for adjusting the 2-D completion percentage surfaces of individual teams and quarterbacks based on the number of their pass attempts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{\\text{adj}}': 'adjusted pass completion probability, dimensionless', 'N_{\\text{comp}, xy}': 'number of completed passes at (x,y), count', 'N_{\\text{att}, xy}': 'total pass attempts at (x,y), count', '\\alpha': 'smoothing parameter, dimensionless', '|\\mathcal{X}|': 'size of spatial domain, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Conditional independence of pass outcomes across spatial bins; uniform prior distribution over pass types.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient pass attempts in sparse regions leading to overfitting.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically maps observed pass counts to adjusted Bayesian posteriors under conjugate priors.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior variance of estimated pass success rates across spatial bins.

primitives.name: Image Processing Toolkit
primitives.verbatim_quote: First, we introduce an image processing tool designed specifically for extracting the raw data from the NGS pass chart images.
primitives.assumptions: Pass chart images are rendered with consistent resolution and color coding.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Poor image quality or non-standard rendering leads to misalignment of extracted points.

layer2.mapping: Extracts pixel-to-coordinate mappings from visual NGS charts using computer vision algorithms.
layer2.telemetry: Root mean square error between extracted coordinates and ground-truth tracking data.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in bridging public-private data gaps in NFL analytics through image-based extraction of tracking data. The primary operator, Pass Completion Probability Surface, models how completion likelihood varies spatially using generalized additive models. It assumes smooth variation in outcomes across field positions and leverages aggregated NGS data. The secondary operator, Naive Bayes Adjustment Model, corrects for small-sample bias in localized pass statistics by applying Bayesian smoothing—this is critical because raw counts can be unreliable in sparse regions. The third operator, Image Processing Toolkit, enables extraction of raw data from static NGS charts, ensuring reproducibility and accessibility. These operators form a layered pipeline where image processing feeds into statistical modeling, which then supports strategic inference. Dualities emerge in that the same spatial coordinates are used both for visualization and modeling, while failure modes include overfitting in low-count zones and misalignment in image preprocessing steps. The methodological rigor ensures robustness against noise in public datasets.
